articles.title: Wrexham 1-2 Birmingham: Phil Neumann's double extends Red Dragons' winless start to Championship season
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wrexham and Birmingham City at the Racecourse Ground; defender Phil Neumann scored either side of a Callum Doyle equaliser to earn victory for Chris Davies' Blues
articles.body:
Centre-back Phil Neumann - who has never scored more than two goals in a single season - scored both Blues goals, either side of a Callum Doyle equaliser.

It was the ideal response from Chris Davies' side, following their 6-1 hammering at the hands of Brentford in the Carabao Cup in midweek.

The Blues deservedly established a lead after 13 minutes, when Neumann headed in Alex Cochrane's header at the far post, but few could deny it should have been 3-0 at the break.

Before the opener, Ollie Rathbone was in the right place at the right time to block August Priske's header from point-blank range, while after it, Jay Stansfield stepped on to Carlos Vicente's neat cut-back and inexplicably powered a shot past the right-hand post when it looked easier to score.

Wrexham generated just 0.22 xG in the first half, but came out with more bite after the break and were rewarded when Lewis O'Brien's dipping cross was helped past James Beadle by Callum Doyle.

But the lead lasted less than 10 minutes. Priske launched a long throw in from the right and recycled it when the first delivery was cleared, finding Neumann, who glanced a header past Anthony Patterson.

Wrexham upped the tempo as the final whistle approached, but they could not find the goal that would have haunted Birmingham.

7: OFF THE LINE ! August Priske has the goal gaping in front of him, but he heads at Wrexham's Ollie Rathbone.

13: GOAL ! Alex Cochrane sends an inswinging corner to the far post, where Phil Neumann heads over the line from close range.

23: HUGE MISS ! Carlos Vicente chops the ball to Jay Stansfield on his right after an overload, but the forward blasts over the bar.

37: SAVE ! Wrexham's best chance of the first half. Danny Imray drives in from the right, with his deflected shot well saved by a diving James Beadle.

54: GOAL ! Lewis O'Brien's brilliant cross dips perfectly for Callum Doyle to equalise.

63: GOAL ! Priske recycles a clearance and finds Neumann, who glances in his second of the night.

77: SO CLOSE ! Let-off for Birmingham. Kieffer Moore's header is not held by James Beadle and only some brave defending from Christoph Klarer prevents a killer Wrexham connection.

Parkinson bemoans "softest two goals conceded in all my time at Wrexham"

Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson speaking on Sky Sports:

"The two goals we conceded are two of the softest goals we've conceded in all my time here - and that includes being in the National League. You can't concede goals like that and expect to win a game of football.

"You've got to defend the box - it's as simple as that - in any division, but particularly the Championship we've got to defend our box better, head the ball out, defend set-plays.

"I thought we lacked conviction in our play tonight in the first half, I've got to be honest. Second half, I thought we were better, got the goal back, and that's why I'm so annoyed with the second goal because we'd started really well, got back in the game.

"We almost looked like a team of everyone looking around the pitch for someone else to go and make it happen, rather than taking responsibility as individuals.

"In football, you can't feel sorry for yourself and I felt we looked like that tonight for some reason. You cannot feel sorry for yourself because no one else is going to help you, you can only help yourself. We've got to look long and hard at ourselves and come out fighting at Millwall."

Birmingham manager Chris Davies speaking on Sky Sports:

"It was a really good night for us. I thought we started the game really well, just like you want to away from home. We got on the front foot, had some moments we could've been maybe a couple of goals up at half-time, so I was really pleased with that.

"I think we looked like a team, that's the main thing. We looked like a real team, and we had to be to come to a place like Wrexham and play a really solid, really good side, especially at home. It's a big, big win."

Do Wrexham need to sign more players before Deadline Day?

"They possibly need a more dominant centre-half, which is something they had during that run through the leagues they had.

"Looking at tonight [2-1 defeat to Birmingham] sometimes it takes a performance or scenarios like this to maybe jog the hierarchy.

"One thing I'm sure Phil Parkinson will say is that he's been backed to the hilt by that ownership group in terms of what he feels he needs to move the club on.

"I'm sure they will feel there's enough there, but I'm sure with Phil, questions will be getting asked in the next few days."

articles.title: Morata, un capitán de España en Segunda
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Dos años después de levantar como capitán de España la Eurocopa, Morata, descontento en el Como, ha dado la sorpresa al fichar por el Leganés, en Segunda División. Se puede hacer extraño, pero conviene recordar antes que nada que hay precedentes sonados a este movimiento. El glorioso Telmo Zarra alargó su carrera primero en el Indautxu y luego en el Barakaldo por mera afición, como hace ahora Morata, y Cruyff fichó en la 1980-81 por el Levante, si bien por motivos menos, digamos, edificantes sino meramente recaudatorios. En ambos casos su presencia en ese segundo escalón agitó positivamente al club escogido y llenó los campos que visitaba. Cruyff incluso llegó a pedir en Vitoria parte de la taquilla bajo amenaza de no jugar, puesto que la gran asistencia se debía a él. En este tiempo hay maneras más lucidas y mejor remuneradas de apearse del fútbol mayor, por ejemplo Arabia y Estados Unidos, donde tenemos ejemplos muy connotados, pero Morata tenía interés en vivir en Madrid por razones estrictamente personales. Su agente, Juanma López, habló con el Atlético, el Rayo y el Getafe, pero no lo vieron, así que se dirigió al Leganés. Ya oigo a quienes dicen que es arrastrarse. Yo más bien pienso que es apurar su afición al fútbol, cuya práctica no se puede recuperar si se abandona. Parar es una decisión sin retorno, él quiere jugar, al Leganés le sirve, así que adelante. Por otra parte, es un futbolista con el que nunca hemos sido quizá del todo justos. Buen jugador, de sacrificio en la brecha, bastante gol y excelente compañero (Luis de la Fuente lo consideró un capitán ideal) había en él algo en su expresión quejumbrosa y cierto aire de niño de casa rica que echaba para atrás al aficionado de pelo en pecho. Pasó por formidables equipos, pero siempre pareció que le faltara una peseta para el duro, por lo que se movió de club con mucha frecuencia sin dejar un gran arraigo. El equipo en el que realmente fue pieza sólida, convincente y duradera ha sido la Selección, donde colmó su carrera. Ahora se enrola en nuestra Segunda División, que enriquece su cartel gracias a este paso del Leganés.

articles.title: Luis Suárez y el Sporting CP enseñan los dientes
articles.standfirst: Doblete del punta colombiano en la goleada sobre Rio Ave (0-4) saldada en la primera parte
articles.summary: Doblete del punta colombiano en la goleada sobre Rio Ave (0-4) saldada en la primera parte
articles.body: El inesperado empate contra Estrela Amadora en la jornada inaugural de la Primeira Liga arrojó ciertas dudas sobre la reconstrucción que debía llevar a cabo Rui Borges a los mandos de un Sporting CP que ha perdido Diomande, Hjulmand, Quenda y Trincao. Sin embargo, se repusieron ante Vitória Guimaraes, se entonaron frente al Alverca... y han sacado los dientes contra Rio Ave (0-4). Sergi Altimira, fijo en el centro del campo, volvió a escoltar a Issa Doumbia y Rodrigo Zalazar... mientras que Fresneda repitió como lateral derecho. La presencia de Flávio Gonçalves (2007) en el once del Sporting CP ya no constituye una sorpresa. El canterano de los 'leones' ha irrumpido con fuerza en los planes de Rui Borges y no hay quien le mueva. Ante el Vitória Guimaraes anotó su primer gol con el primer equipo del Sporting CP... y apenas le llevó cinco minutos repetir ante Río Ave. Le dibujó el desmarque a Issa Doumbia entre central y lateral para terminar definiendo con delicadeza al palo largo con un disparo raso. No se quedó ahí y, antes de llegar al minuto 20, asistió a Catamo con un pase de 'trivela'. El Sporting CP quería dejar el encuentro resuelto antes de marcharse al descanso... y ahí fue donde apareció Luis Suárez para anotar un doblete en cuestión de 10'. Primero, recogió un rechace de Catamo al palo y posteriormente, culminó con la zurda desde fuera del área una gran jugada colectiva llevada de lado a lado.

articles.title: Aday Mara: un debut muy protagonista
articles.standfirst: El pívot jugó 19 minutos y tuvo una gran actuación
articles.summary: El pívot jugó 19 minutos y tuvo una gran actuación
articles.body: Aunque había dos jugadores zaragozanos en el pabellón (el otro era Jaime Pradilla), la mayor parte de las ovaciones se las llevó, Aday Mara, que se estrenaba con la selección y tuvo casi todos los focos del partido. El de los Thunder debutó cuando se llevaban jugados 6:38 del partido, y poco después firmó un 2+1 muy celebrado en el Príncipe Felipe. Mucho más ruido hubo cuando clavó un mate en un contraataque. Aday liquidó su estreno con 12 puntos, 6 rebotes, 4 tapones y 17 de valoración en 19 minutos. Jugó el tramo final, en el que se decidió el partido y mantuvo un duelo con Neemias Queta fabuloso del que saltaron chispas. “Estoy muy contento con el debut, un poco nerviosillo al principio, pero creo que he hecho un buen trabajo ante un jugador NBA como Queta. Lo malo ha sido la derrota, así que toca ponerse serios, aprender de los errores y centrarse en el partido ante Grecia”, fueron las palabras del gran protagonista de la noche por su debut. El otro jugador que ya tiene en su palmarés un partido oficial con la selección es Baba Miller. Será importante en el futuro, pero ante Portugal no tuvo casi incidencia. Salió a 8:11 para el final del segundo cuarto, jugó cinco minutos y se fue sin anotar, con un tiro fallado tanto de dos como de tres, una asistencia y un rebote.

articles.title: Derek McInnes backs himself to deliver Rangers success after 'tough start'
articles.summary: Manager Derek McInnes says Rangers are "a long way away" from what he wants but backs himself to deliver success at Ibrox.
articles.body:
Manager Derek McInnes says Rangers are "a long way away" from what he wants but backs himself to deliver success at Ibrox.

The 55-year-old oversaw a second exit from European competition this season with a Conference League play-off defeat on penalties by Czech side Jablonec.

Domestically, Rangers have progressed in the League Cup and will host Celtic in the quarter-finals next month but McInnes' side have picked up just one point from their opening two Scottish Premiership matches and visit Aberdeen on Sunday.

"I like to think I know what I'm doing as a manager, I'm a good manager, I back myself but at the minute, none of us are doing our job well enough," McInnes told Sky Sports.

"The players need a wee bit of help and support at the minute.

"We're a long way away from the Rangers team that I want us to be and the Rangers team that I intend us to be. The players are working extremely hard.

"There's a lot of uncertainty at the minute. Once the window closes, everything becomes a bit calmer."

Rangers to give Celtic 300 tickets for cup game

Rangers count consequences of European failure

Twelve players have been recruited already and McInnes hopes to sign "a couple more" and expects "one or two" to leave before the closure of the transfer window next week.

"We've obviously missed big Youssef [Chermiti, who is injured], the type of striker to go and stretch teams.

"I don't expect us to be perfect at this stage. It's not been the start we wanted, I'm not the first Rangers manager to get off to a tough start but we are determined to follow this job through and it's the end that counts and I still believe we're going to be a success here."

After Thursday's match, McInnes lamented his side's struggle to be either possession-based, counter attacking or direct.

"My teams have always had some sort of identity," explained the former Aberdeen, Hearts, Kilmarnock and St Johnstone manager.

"I want us to try and be a team that puts more stress on teams defensively and I don't think that we are at the minute.

"We've got good ball players and I think we just need to relax a wee bit more in possession and be comfortable with what we're try to do. It's not as if we're not capable of being that but I do think with an extra one or two additions, it will help us become something.

"I want us to be able to be a team that goes full press but when you go full press and you're aggressive, you've got to be really aggressive with that and you've got to pick up second balls and win duels and turn the ball over and really impose yourself on the game.

"There's talented players here. You don't get in the door at Rangers unless you're a talented player."

articles.title: Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City: Rayan Cherki impresses in big away win
articles.summary: After two goals and a swaggering display against Crystal Palace, Phil McNulty asks if this is Rayan Cherki's time to shine for Manchester City.
articles.body:
Rayan Cherki refuses to hide his emotions, an open book for all to see and hear in times of joy and disappointment.

Moments after Manchester City had put down their first heavyweight marker of the post-Pep Guardiola era by brushing aside Crystal Palace , he was asked live on TV how much he enjoyed the game. Rather than providing the usual textbook answer, he instead gave a colourfully uncomplimentary – and unprintable - description of his own first-half performance.

Erling Haaland, standing alongside Cherki as he waited to hand over the player-of-the-match award, could only laugh at the France attacker's sweary honesty.

Indeed, the 23-year-old also refuses to hide his talent, making a nonsense of his self-criticism by unveiling a Selhurst Park masterclass with two brilliant second-half goals in the 4-1 victory.

Cherki made his impact under Guardiola last season, although there was always a feeling the mercurial signing from Lyon for a bargain £30m could produce more. He made 33 Premier League appearances - but 14 of those were as a substitute.

And there is a sense that he already has something to prove under new boss Enzo Maresca amid City's vast attacking resources, coming off the bench to assist the two late goals that gave them victory against Bournemouth on the opening weekend.

Cherki was seen in animated conversation with Maresca after the final whistle, but his reward was a start at Selhurst Park and he delivered the sort of irresistible performance he, as well as City, needed.

Cherki inspires Man City to comfortable win at Palace

Cherki genius and Wharton excels - Palace v Man City player ratings

He had a disappointing World Cup with France, reduced to a bit-part player, only starting against England in the third-fourth place play-off, being replaced at half-time with his side 4-0 down.

There were also videos that emerged with Cherki showing apparent displeasure at coach Didier Deschamps.

Cherki has a reputation for unpredictability, with Maresca saying after his contribution against Bournemouth that "if he is not happy he wants to show it".

But, though he has proved hard to please in the past at Leicester City and Chelsea , Maresca was satisfied with Cherki here.

"He's happy and I'm happy," said Maresca. "It was not just his performance with the two goals, but his work off the ball.

"He pressed and gave us a complete performance on the ball and off the ball.

"Rayan is Rayan. We know him. He loves football and it makes it so much easier to work with him.

"The quality he has in this moment helps the team, not just with assists but goals."

It was not just Cherki's wizardry with the ball that impressed Maresca, but his work off it.

"His performance off the ball was unbelievable," he added to BBC Match of the Day. "Everyone knows his quality but when he works hard off the ball, he was in charge of Adam Wharton. He controlled him. He was very good."

Praise indeed as the outstanding Wharton is one of the players City have cast their eyes over as they try to strengthen Maresca's squad before the close of the transfer window.

For all the team work that brought such praise from Maresca, it was the two moments of individual genius that will be remembered after a win and performance that suggested talk that City will inevitably go into decline after the departure of Guardiola has been greatly exaggerated.

He also produced those defining moments at crucial times, the first coming nine minutes into the second half with City leading 1-0 and Palace hoping to mount a recovery.

Cherki took Phil Foden's pass on the edge of the area, embarking on a slalom run surrounded by four Palace defenders, leaving them helpless before poking a left-foot finish past keeper Dean Henderson.

He celebrated with a touch of arrogance that is so often the preserve of the special ones, staring down the Palace fans on the Holmesdale Road end.

And after Palace pulled one back, it was Cherki who once again restored that two-goal advantage with a rising right-foot shot from 20 yards past Henderson.

Former England midfielder Jamie Redknapp told Sky Sports: "After Rayan Cherki painted a masterpiece, City started to play and got a real hold of it.

"Cherki felt like the difference because his goals came at an important time. He is a genius. The things he can do with a football are absolute genius.

"There aren't many Premier League players I've seen that can do this on the first goal.

"Eden Hazard possibly, he was that kind of player. Georgi Kinkladze, there'll be Manchester City fans from a previous generation who'll remember him, who could get past people in a telephone box. This was very similar.

"Once Cherki is in the box, they are so scared to touch him. It's absolute genius. He's an absolute bargain at £30m and gives you a new dimension. He gives you that 'X-factor'. He does things differently.

Cherki's goal celebrations summed up his confidence and attitude, with Redknapp saying: "There was a bit of Cantona about him. He's a beautiful player. With someone like Cherki you've got to let him do his thing."

There may be ups and downs between the maverick Cherki and the demanding Maresca, but the France star with stardust in his boots showed he will not be pushed to the back of the queue among City's array of attacking talent – with perhaps more to come before the deadline.

And that is good news for Maresca as he tried to build on the foundations left behind by Guardiola.

articles.title: El Sevilla vuelve a preguntar por Zeballos
articles.standfirst: Tras la venta de Oso y la posible marcha de Vargas, el extremo de Boca Juniors reaparece como opción para el extremo
articles.summary: Tras la venta de Oso y la posible marcha de Vargas, el extremo de Boca Juniors reaparece como opción para el extremo
articles.body: Se avecina una intensa recta final del mercado de fichajes en el Sevilla. Con el traspaso de Oso al Estrasburgo encarrilado por 10 millones de euros y la más que probable salida de Rubén Vargas, ahora la dirección deportiva tiene como una de sus prioridades reforzar las bandas, donde los nervionenses de momento solamente cuentan con Alfon, Chidera Ejuke y Miguel Sierra para las posiciones de extremo. En una lista de candidatos donde se han barajado opciones como Bryan Zaragoza -fichado por el Espanyol-, Bryan Gil o Gabri Martínez, vuelve a emerger el nombre del argentino Exequiel Zeballos, que ya sonó el pasado verano. Según apunta el periodista Nicolò Schira, el Sevilla se habría interesado por Exequiel Zeballos, por el que ya preguntó durante los primeros meses de Matías Almeyda en el banquillo blanquirrojo. Tal como señala esta información, el Parma ha presentado una oferta de 5 millones por el futbolista de 24 años, pero Boca Juniors la considera insuficiente. El Changuito termina contrato con el club xeneize el próximo mes de diciembre y ha rechazado todas las propuestas de renovación, provocando que el presidente, Juan Román Riquelme, decida que se entrene al margen de la plantilla, perdiéndose los seis primeros partidos del campeonato argentino. Si bien el Celta de Vigo también llegó a tantear la incorporación de Exequiel Zeballos hace algunas semanas, los gallegos terminaron descartando esta vía ante la prioridad del jugador de marcharse al Nápoles, uniéndose el Bolonia y el Parma también a la puja. Sin embargo, las negociaciones con la entidad partenopea se han estancado debido a sus limitaciones al inscribir nuevos futbolistas, abriéndose una ventana de oportunidad para varios clubes, entre ellos el propio Sevilla.

articles.title: Jerry Sandusky accuser set to recant testimony, claims statements were made under 'extreme psychological and institutional pressure'
articles.summary: Sandusky will reportedly have an evidentiary hearing on Sept. 8 reviewing a signed affidavit from one of his accusers.
articles.body:
One of the 10 people who accused former Penn State defensive coordinator Jerry Sandusky of abuse is set to recant his testimony, according to court documents obtained by multiple media outlets.

Sandusky, 82, is reportedly set to appear in court in Bellefonte, Pennsylvania, next month for an evidentiary hearing that will review the accuser's recanted testimony. The hearing will take place Sept. 8.

According to a signed affidavit from June 30, 2025, the accuser known as Victim 10 in the trial alleges that he was "misled repeatedly" by prosecutors.

"I now regret my role in facilitating what I have come to view as a deeply flawed prosecution," Victim 10 wrote.

In the statement, Victim 10 called out prosecutor Joe McGettigan as someone who influenced his testimony; McGettigan, who was the lead prosecutor on the case, died in December.

Victim 10 wrote that he was "repeatedly encouraged" to believe that he had been abused by Sandusky, despite a "lack of clear or certain memory of any such conduct." The accuser said that he was "coached" during pretrial meetings, including one that lasted around six hours, and asked to "reframe" his account "until my responses aligned with what appeared to be desired by the prosecution team."

"Throughout the pretrial process, I was told — both directly and indirectly — that trauma may have fragmented my memory, and that I could safely affirm details I did not fully recall. I was assured this was common and even expected," he wrote. "Over time, my story changed. My testimony evolved. This evolution was not deliberate deception but the result of emotional strain, repeated exposure to leading questions, intense investigative pressure, and psychological manipulation."

Victim 10 said he did not commit perjury, saying that his statements "were not willfully false, but induced under extreme psychological and institutional pressure."

Victim 10 said he received $5.5 million in the civil settlement from the trial. He also said he was promised that his identity would be kept confidential, which he said did not end up being the case.

In a motion to seek a new trial obtained by multiple outlets, Sandusky's defense team said that Victim 10's now-estranged wife would testify that Victim 10 initially denied that he had been abused by Sandusky.

In a statement to ABC News , prosecutors with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's office dismissed the opinion of Victim 10's ex "thirteen years after defendant's trial, pondering what she thinks may or may not have really happened to [Victim 10] when he was 10 years old" as "irrelevant and inadmissible."

Sandusky, a former Nittany Lion defensive end, coached at Penn State from 1969 to 1999. The accusations of abuse are related to Sandusky's charity, The Second Mile, which he founded in 1977.

Sandusky was arrested in 2011 and convicted of 45 counts of child sexual abuse in 2012. He was sentenced to 30-60 years in prison, a sentence that was re-affirmed in 2019 after his lawyers' bid for a new trial was denied.

The scandal had wide-ranging effects on the university's football program. Legendary head coach Joe Paterno was fired in the wake of the accusations; he died in January 2012, and a statue of him outside Beaver Stadium was taken down the following July.

articles.title: Todd McShay Explains Ranking Arch Manning as 5th-Best QB in 2027 NFL Draft Class in Video
articles.summary: NFL draft analyst Todd McShay doesn't think Texas' Arch Manning is heading into the 2026 season as a top-four college football quarterback.
articles.body:
NFL draft analyst Todd McShay doesn't think Texas' Arch Manning is heading into the 2026 season as a top-four college football quarterback.

McShay said in a recent appearance on The Ryen Russillo Show he currently has Manning ranked as his fifth-ranked quarterback in the 2027 NFL draft class.

McShay named Oregon's Dante Moore and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers as his 1A and 1B quarterbacks in the class.

He added he sees Notre Dame's CJ Carr and LSU's Sam Leavitt as other candidates to become the top quarterback in the class.

Manning is looking to increase his NFL draft stock by building on a first full-time starting season in which he completed 61.4 percent of his passes for 3,163 passing yards with 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

He will kick off his redshirt junior campaign next Saturday, Sept. 5 with a game against visiting Texas State.

articles.title: MTSU Reveals Jersey Patch to Honor Dolly Parton in Photo After Country Music Legend's Death
articles.summary: Middle Tennessee State is honoring late country music icon Dolly Parton with a special patch for the football team's season opener.
articles.body:
Middle Tennessee State is honoring late country music icon Dolly Parton with a special patch for the football team's season opener.

The Blue Raiders will wear a jersey featuring Parton's signature and her birth and death years for next Saturday's home opener against Murray State.

Parton died this week in Nashville at the age of 80.

Middle Tennessee announced the jersey initiative Friday at the university's Center for Popular Music, which features multiple artifacts from Parton's career.

A game-worn jersey featuring the special patch will be donated to the center after the home opener, MTSU athletics director Chris Massaro said .

Massaro said the tribute is especially appropriate because the game takes place on Sept. 5, a date coinciding with Parton's iconic roles in the song and film "9 to 5."

Fans attending the home opener will also be shown QR codes allowing them to donate to the Imagination Library, a program launched by Parton in 1995 which gifts books to children aged zero through five.

Other sports organizations across Parton's state have also shared tributes in the singer and philanthropist's honor, including the University of Tennessee , Tennessee Titans and Nashville Predators .

articles.title: William & Mary Rallies in Final Seconds, Stuns Villanova at the Buzzer in Opener
articles.summary: The Tribe snatched victory from the jaws of defeat in Philly on Friday night.
articles.body:
The Patriot League debut for William & Mary couldn't have gone much better. For #8-ranked Villanova it couldn't have gone much worse. Despite leading by ten points with under a minute to play, the Wildcats collapsed and lost their season opener at home to their league mates that followed them over form the Patriot League. The Tribe are celebrating a win that might just vault them into the rankings and make them a contender in their new conference while 'Nova is left wondering what the heck just happened. The importance of finishing has perhaps never been on full display more than it was in Philadelphia on Friday evening.

The drama, controversy… or whatever it could be called… about quarterback Pat McQuaide's eligibility loomed large over the Wildcats heading in. At what felt like the eleventh hour McQuaide was deemed able to play when it seemed like he wouldn't and it felt as though Villanova should be the shoo-in favorite to win and they were. Mark Ferrante's squad was giving their old CAA-turned-Patriot League rivals 11.5 points and they certainly lived up to that billing early on. McQuaide and the offense scored on their opening possession with a five-yard touchdown run from Isaiah Ragland.

They had the look of a team coming back from making an appearance in the FCS semifinals just eight months ago. That guise, though, would not last long. In fact it only took the Tribe four plays to respond. After two failed run plays, William & Mary quarterback Winston Watkins took to the air. He floated a long 69-yard pass that was hauled in by receiver Carson Jenkins. In a blink the game was tied and it was clear that the Tribe had not come to mess around.

That notion was made even more evident in the second quarter. Mike London's team took a 10-7 lead off the foot of kicker Max Lipinski and then shortly thereafter the defense made its first big play of the night, intercepting McQuaide. Defensive back Cade Ellis came down with the pick, effectively swinging the pendulum of momentum totally to the side of the visitors.

William & Mary was unable to do anything with the turnover, though, and Villanova responded to the adversity well. Following a forced punt, the Wildcats regained the lead with their second TD run of the evening. This one was a 11-yard scamper from Ja'briel Mace to make it 14-10. The score would balloon to 17-10 by the break with a Dominic LeBlanc field goal.

The Tribe fought back hard in the third quarter. Another field goal was followed up by a big defensive stop. Down by four, Watkins and the offense again moved quickly to snatch the lead right back. Aided by a fortuitous own fumble recovery by running back Andrew King, William & Mary scored again when Watkins called his own number and pushed in from a yard out. The ensuing PAT would fail, though, ensuring the score would be 19-17 heading into the fourth quarter. That missed extra point, it turned out, would end up being huge.

The Wildcats continued to falter in the final 15 minutes. Just one play into their first drive of the fourth quarter, Mace fumbled and William & Mary linebacker Harrison Johnson recovered. Watkins went on to orchestrate a 13-play drive that ate up over five minutes. It only ended in a field goal, though, meaning that Villanova was still just one score away.

But then it began to avalanche in a bad way on the Tribe. On their next series, William & Mary gave it right back when sophomore Wildcats DB Jamie Tyson picked off Watkins. Shortly after McQuaide found Brandon Binkowski for the eight-yard score. A subsequent turnover on downs saw Villanova add on again with a 37-yard touchdown run from Ragland. In a flurry of mistakes and big plays, 'Nova led it 32-22 with just 2:43 to go.

Trailing by ten, Watkins and the offense were surprisingly lethargic. They did get down into field goal range for Lipinski but, with a mere 53 seconds left, it seemed like those three points would be inconsequential. All Villanova needed to do was recover the upcoming onside kick. That, though, was a lot easier said than done. Sam Braidwood came in and delivered a line drive stinger that flew by Wildcats receiver Braden Reed. Reed could not fall on it and instead William & Mary got it, much to the dismay of the Wildcats fans.

That dismay turned to agony three plays later when Watkins fired a long pass to Kai Austin. Austin got behind the defense on a blown coverage and corralled the 37-yard tying score. The stadium fell silent save for the celebration of the Tribe sideline. Overtime loomed, or so it seemed. Another massive mistake in the literal final seconds, though, would ensure that even that wouldn't be the case for 'Nova.

McQuaide misread a pass with just five ticks to go and Ellis jumped the route. His second interception of the night was the one that set up the improbable winning score for William & Mary as he returned it back the edge of field goal range. Lipinski came out and nailed the 45-yard attempt, completing the epic comeback.

The Tribe defense forced four takeaways in total and Watkins accounted for over 300 all-purpose yards on the other side. More impressive than any stat, however, was the tremendous amount of overall team grit displayed by William & Mary in those closing minutes. With the game seemingly falling around them, they calmly made play after play and now… in a truly unbelievable manner… they are 1-0 with an early leg up in the Patriot League race.

For Villanova this is about as bad as it gets. Losing a conference (and season) opener to an unranked foe at home in that fashion is brutal and one that will be really hard to rebound from. McQuaide finished his night with 270 passing yards and a score but also had three interceptions. The last, of course, was the final dagger but all three proved costly as did the lost fumble from Mace. Receiver Jake Hinton caught four passes for 132 yards and Ragland toted it 14 times for 94 on the ground. It was all for naught, though, and now they are left to deal with an extremely ugly season-opening loss.

articles.title: Peyton Manning's Son Marshall Injured, Latest News on 2030 QB's Status After HSFB Debut
articles.summary: Marshall Manning, son of Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning, will have to wait to compete in his second high school football game.
articles.body:
Marshall Manning, son of Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning, will have to wait to compete in his second high school football game.

Manning is sidelined by a foot injury that kept him out of his Chattanooga high school's second game of the season, coach Erik Kimrey said Friday (h/t the Chattanooga Times Free Press ' Stephen Hargis).

Kimrey said Manning has "got a foot injury and will be out a few weeks," per Hargis.

A member of the high school graduating class of 2030, Manning plays for Baylor School in Tennessee. He made his high school football debut last Thursday.

Manning played two snaps in a ESPN2-televised game between Baylor School and Brentwood.

He started out his debut with an eight-yard completion to Ole Miss commit Antwaun Adams.

Kimrey said after the season opener he wanted Manning to get reps in every Baylor School game this season, per USA Today's Joseph Spears .

"I want Marshall to play in every game this year, even if it's just two plays like that," Kimrey said last week. "Hopefully it'll be a lot more. We need him next year and he needs to be ready."

Manning is currently backing up Keegan Croucher, a member of the class of 2027 ranked as a top-10 high school quarterback in the nation by 247Sports .

Croucher, who is playing in his final high school season, is a four-star prospect who has been committed since October 2025 to Ole Miss.

Kimrey will hope to get Manning back on the field as soon as he's healthy in order to get him some more experience before he is potentially tasked with taking over for Croucher next fall.

Manning, 15, is the latest member of his family to launch his football career. His cousin Arch is preparing to begin his second season as Texas' full-time starter with a Saturday, Sept. 5 matchup against Texas State.

articles.title: La Liga F Moeve se verá en la tele… y en La Quiniela
articles.standfirst: La competición podrá verse al completo en Dazn, bajo suscripción, y cuatro partidos por jornada en abierto en TVE y TV3
articles.summary: La competición podrá verse al completo en Dazn, bajo suscripción, y cuatro partidos por jornada en abierto en TVE y TV3
articles.body: No es la primera vez que el mal llamado fútbol femenino forma parte de La Quiniela, juego de azar gestionado por Loterías y Apuestas del Estado que se juega desde 1946, pero esta vez parece que ha llegado para quedarse. La primera vez que apareció en un boleto fue el 30 de septiembre de 2017, cuando un Atlético-Athletic fue el Pleno al 15. Aquella temporada volverían a aparecer de manera esporádica (Athletic-Barcelona en la jornada 12; Valencia-Betis en la jornada 20; o Madrid CFF-Barcelona en la jornada 46), si bien el plato fuerte fue el boleto del 11 de marzo de 2018 que contó con siete encuentros de la por entonces llamada Liga Femenina Iberdrola en un acto enmarcado en el Día Internacional de la Mujer. Después de aquello, la llegada de la Liga F a La Quniela ha sido un canto de sirena hasta que el pasado 6 de mayo se publicara en el BOE la actualización de la norma que rige esta Ley (13/2011). Un paso más importante que la simple visibilidad, pues la LPFF entra en el reparto de la recaudación, correspondiéndole un 15% del 22% de la recaudación total. Según datos aportados por AFE, gran impulsor de esta demanda, se estima que los clubes podrían sumar alrededor de 10 millones de euros. La Liga F Moeve cumplirá su quinta temporada en Dazn después de que la plataforma británica rubricara un nuevo contrato por tres temporadas para emitir todos los partidos de cada jornada. Según datos ofrecidos por Liga F, la competición alcanzó la temporada pasada una audiencia acumulada de 7.5 millones de espectadores, con un incremento del 11.2% respecto a la anterior y del 127% desde la creación de Liga F en la campaña 2022/23. Esto se debe, en gran parte, a la entrada en juego de TVE y TV3, entes públicos que también vuelven a ser adjudicatarios de los derechos para emitir en abierto hasta cuatro partidos por jornada. Uno de los grandes debes de la Liga F Moeve es la asistencia a los estadios. Aunque el año pasado hubo hasta 71 partidos disputados en grandes recintos, un 30% más que el curso anterior, la cifra media habría descendido ligeramente colocándose en los 1.400 aficionados.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola: Liverpool agree £123m deal for PSG forward
articles.summary: Liverpool are closing in on a deal to sign forward Bradley Barcola, which will increase doubts over Cody Gakpo's future.
articles.body:
Liverpool have agreed a deal worth up to £123m for Paris St-Germain forward Bradley Barcola.

PSG initially valued the France attacker at £145m, but the Reds have agreed a package worth an initial £106m with £17m in potential add-ons.

The 23-year-old is expected to have a medical this weekend before signing a long-term contract at Anfield.

Right-footed Barcola prefers to play on the left wing and his impending arrival will increase the doubts around Cody Gakpo's future at Liverpool .

Multiple sources have told BBC Sport both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City have shown interest in the Netherlands forward.

Liverpool are also in the market for a right winger, having explored moves for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr.

Barcola has become a main target for Liverpool as they look to bolster their attack following the departures of Luis Diaz and Mohamed Salah in the past two summers.

He moved to PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported £38.5m and has won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, the French Cup twice, as well as the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.

Barcola, who scored three goals for France in this summer's World Cup, can also play on the right or through the middle and could provide cover for Alexander Isak while Hugo Ekitike recovers from a serious Achilles injury.

Speaking before Saturday's game against Nottingham Forest (12:30 BST), Reds boss Andoni Iraola was asked about Gakpo's future and said he "cannot guarantee anything", but wants to keep the 27-year-old at the club.

"[Gakpo] has been very good since he came back from the World Cup and his holiday, with a very good attitude. I hope we can keep him at that level because I think he has been very influential in our games," Iraola he said.

The strengths Barcola will bring to Anfield

Analysis: Deal makes sense for both teams

Barcola has been a priority for Liverpool since Yan Diomande opted to join Real Madrid earlier in the window. The Frenchman's move to Anfield - for up to £123m - would be a record fee for a player leaving Ligue 1.

Barcola will bring star factor and inject real quality into a Liverpool attack that could become feared if last summer's expensive signings Isak and Florian Wirtz can step up.

PSG can feasibly look at the deal as an excellent outcome, given they signed Barcola for £38m and will more than triple their money - if add-ons are met - for a player who is entering the last two years of his contract and has shown no willingness to sign an extension.

Barcola was often behind Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the wings in the biggest games last season and PSG have added to their options in those areas this summer by signing Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts.

However Liverpool will be pleased with the deal too, having held firm earlier in the summer in terms of meeting PSG's valuation of £145m - but eventually bringing in one of Europe's most exciting forwards.

articles.title: Scottish gossip: Van den Berg, Spencer, Sigur, Ugresic, Mahmic, Fofana
articles.summary: Celtic are reportedly close to signing PSV Eindhoven's Joel van den Berg, but they and Rangers appear to have missed out on other targets as Dundee United consider another bid for Falkirk's Brad Spencer.
articles.body:
Celtic are reportedly close to signing PSV Eindhoven's Joel van den Berg, but they and Rangers appear to have missed out on other targets as Dundee United consider another bid for Falkirk's Brad Spencer.

A Celtic delegation is in the Netherlands to discuss the acquisition of midfielder Joel van den Berg, with the 19-year-old open to a transfer having yet to become a first-team regular with PSV Eindoven . ( VI , external )

PSV Eindhoven seem poised to sell Joel van den Berg to Celtic after the midfielder was pulled out of the Jong PSV side for their second-tier match with RKC Waalwijk on Friday, according to Dutch journalist Rik Elfrink. ( Glasgow Times , external )

Hajduk Split head coach Gonzalez Garcia has confirmed Celtic target Niko Sigur has played his last game for the club, but although the 22-year-old midfielder is reportedly keen to join the Scottish Champions, they face competition from Genk and Toulouse . ( The National , external )

Partizan Belgrade president Rasim Ljajic says they rejected a bid from Celtic for playmaker Ognjen Ugresic because they had already given their word to PAOK to sell the 20-year-old for £400,000 less than the Scottish champions offered. ( Mozzart Sport , external )

articles.standfirst: Toni Fernández se va al Venezia por 5 millones y Ávaro Cortés al Amberes por 3,5
articles.summary: Toni Fernández se va al Venezia por 5 millones y Ávaro Cortés al Amberes por 3,5
articles.body: El Barcelona sigue trabajando con la idea de vender a los jugadores jóvenes formados en La Masía que no tienen sitio en el primer equipo. Desde hace unos años, Deco ha intensificado este tipo de operaciones con el fin de rentabilizar el talento que hay en el fútbol base culé. Y esto es lo que ha sucedido con Toni Fernández y Álvaro Cortés. El club azulgrana ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Venezia para el traspaso de Toni Fernández. El club italiano pagará cinco millones de euros. El Barcelona se guarda un porcentaje de una futura venta y tiene también una opción de recompra. El acuerdo es total y, en este momento, se están redactando los contratos antes de la firma definitiva. En esta misma situación se encuentra la salida de Álvaro Cortés al Amberes. El acuerdo es total y solamente queda la firma. El defensa se marcha traspasado al club belga por 3,5 millones de euros. Al igual que en el caso de Toni Fernández, el club azulgrana se guarda una opción de recompra y un porcentaje de una futura venta. El anuncio oficial de estos dos traspasos no será inminente. La operación que, presumiblemente, se hará oficial este sábado es el traspaso de Héctor Fort a la Real Sociedad por ocho millones de euros. El club se queda con el 50 % de sus derechos.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | 'Last three years of my career have been the most transformative': Bengaluru FC's Ryan Williams
articles.summary: Football News: Ryan Williams arrived in India as an Australian footballer looking for a new challenge. Three years later, the Bengaluru FC winger has become one of t.
articles.body: Ryan Williams arrived in India as an Australian footballer looking for a new challenge. Three years later, the Bengaluru FC winger has become one of the Indian national team's most vocal advocates, embracing both the club and the country as home.The 32-year-old has experienced near misses with Bengaluru FC, adapting to Indian football, and the responsibility of mentoring younger players while representing India. Despite a six-year trophy drought at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium, he believes the club is closer to success than results suggest.In this conversation with TimesofIndia.com, Williams, who was roped in by JSW Sports recently, speaks about Bengaluru FC's title ambitions, manager Pep Muñoz's philosophy, the OCI debate, national team pride, and why life in Bengaluru has been an enjoyable chapter of his career.Excerpts:Q. Can you start by talking about your time so far in India, move to Bengaluru FC, playing for the national team?Ryan: Yeah, probably the last three years of my career has been the most, first and foremost, transformative, I would say, definitely. But also the one I've enjoyed the most with kind of what I'm doing with BFC, although we haven't won anything.My everyday life here, I love it. I love living in Bangalore, the football club itself, the way the club is run.Then obviously moving on to the national team has been such an amazing experience for me. It's one that has been so positive and hopefully I can continue to keep it in a positive way and just try and help the younger boys, try and, if possible, get more players like me to do what I've done, for me to show them it is possible. I've said in many interviews that if there is anything I can do, please reach out. And I've had boys reach out, which is good because obviously the reason I'm here is to help Indian football at the end of the day.Q. Let me start off by focusing on Bengaluru FC. Six-year title drought. Does the pressure tell on you that the team hasn't won in so long?Ryan: Not at all. I don't think so at all. I think it's more the fans who have been here to enjoy the super successful times. We have been slowly building and almost got there. The season before I came, they got to three finals. And then the season after, we had a managerial change. Then the season after that, we got to the ISL Cup final. And from our own doing, we couldn't hold out.Obviously last season, with it being a truncated season, just when we kind of found our feet, the season finished. So this season will be really exciting. I don't feel any pressure personally.The fans are amazing. They obviously stick with us through the good and the bad. They're probably the best fans in India in terms of how they do stick behind us when things aren't going so well. So for us, it's more about trying to give them something back. That's how I see it, because they've been so amazing with us, especially with me having come over here from Australia and everything that's come in between.The hardest thing to do as a men's professional footballer is to win trophies. And that's something that, you know, the last three seasons we haven't done since I've been here. So it's definitely something that we've spoken about and something that we want to put right.Q. When you joined Bengaluru FC, it's not just about joining a very professional team, but also about adapting to Indian football. How tricky has that experience been in navigating not just things on the field, but off the field?Ryan: I'm a pretty well-travelled guy. I moved to the UK by myself when I was 16, moved in with a foster family, had to figure all that out by myself and then back to Australia and then India. So it was difficult the kind of first six to eight weeks in terms of outside of football. But then after that, I kind of found my feet and understood how things worked.And there's still things that I'm not quite 100 percent on, but, you know, I've got a good network of people supporting me, which definitely helped. And then in terms of football, I think any new club you go to, especially a different country as well. I mean, I look back on my first season and towards the end, I started to come through and started to be more confident and got used to the players I'm with, got used to the surroundings, the pitches, even the day to day.I would say one thing that helped me on the pitch was having Simon Grayson (Bengaluru FC manager from 2022 until 23) and his management staff because they were all English and they took the sessions and organised everything the way that I was used to for 12 years in England. So that was a massive help for me. But it did take me the first half of the season to really find my feet and then started to enjoy my football at the end.And then I just kind of kept going, kept believing in myself and got used to (it). Because the European players are obviously different to Indian players and there's positives and negatives about both. So it's trying to work out how do I communicate in a proper way. They all do speak English, that's not the issue. In the UK, you can kind of shout and scream at people and they listen to the message and not how the message is given. Whereas here you have to be more cautious about how you give the message rather than what the message is sometimes. And that's one thing I've been trying to help the young boys with. Just trying to be more positive around them and let them that I'm here to support you. We're both on the same team. We're trying to go for the same thing. So it's in my best interest to help them perform at their maximum capability. In turn, if we win something because of him, everybody wins. So that was one thing that I had to kind of figure out in the first six months.Q. Ahead of the next season, manager Pep Munoz spoke about having a strong defensive structure and then allowing the wings to come into play. What do you make of the style and the approach that the manager is trying to instil within the club?Ryan: I really like it. I was lucky enough to work with Gerard (Zaragoza) and Sebas (Sebastian Vega) before who have a similar approach... the Spanish management style, which I was new to at first when Gerard came in. So it's put me in good stead because we spent a year and a half or thereabouts together.We want people that wear the jersey with pride and are willing to give everything to play for the country. I think that is what it means to play for your country.And last season was good in a way that he [Muñoz] came in. He came in with his coaching staff and it was really good because everybody got to kind of figure out how to work with each other, what exactly he wants to do on the pitch. And that's put us in good stead for this season because last season was, for lack of better words, almost like a draft copy. It was like a dummy run. So now we've been in pre-season early, we're spending a lot more time on the pitch, figuring out exactly what he wants and how we can best do that on the pitch to obviously give us results, put people in positions that works best for everybody. So I'm really excited.I really love what he's doing on the football pitch. And the good thing is that obviously that small part we had with him last season has been, like I said, a dummy run to push us forward into this season. So we don't need as much time together on the grass to connect the dots. The dots are connected and now it's just about fine tuning it and pushing it forward.Q. There is consideration about bringing in a Sports Passport or allowing more OCIs. What do you make of that consideration?Ryan: I think for Indian football, for it to grow at a faster rate than what it is now, we need to see success in the national team. And if that means that the Sports Passport and the OCI can help us in the next one to two years to push us up higher up the rankings and get us qualified for Asian Cups and stuff like that, then there's going to be more interest in Indian football. That's great, but I think long term, I think it would work. I think if we can send the younger boys from here that way, rather than bringing them this way, if that makes sense.Q. Is that a chicken and egg sort of situation? Because if you don't succeed, if the national team does not succeed, then the number of players who would want to give up their passports will also be lesser. Or does it work the other way around?Ryan: If they're looking at just coming here when it [national team] does good, I think maybe they're the wrong kind of people we're looking for. I think we want players that want to come here, give everything for the country and help the national team. And within helping the national team, we actually help the whole ecosystem. So, you know, like for me, there was no guarantees of anything. I have kind of done it because that's what I wanted to do. I'm proud to play for India. There has to be that pride.We want people that wear the jersey with pride and are willing to give everything to play for the country. I think that's what it means to play for your country.Q. What have you liked about Bengaluru as city and the culture? And is there a connect between all the cities you've lived in the past?Ryan: There's no city that I've lived in that's like Bengaluru. You know, it is in itself its own kind of country, if you will. Like, first of all, I love the weather. The weather is perfect. If you came straight from the UK, you're in heaven because you have these nice periods where it's nice and cool, like it is now in the rain. And then in the summer, it's nice and warm, but not too hot.You know, the kind of the restaurants here, which my wife and I try to go to as much as possible. There's just so much to do. There's so much to see. There's, you know, so many different aspects to this city that make it beautiful and I really love it all.For me, it's a very relaxed lifestyle. And that's kind of how I like to live my life, in a very relaxed, laidback, not taking things too seriously way. And I feel like here's the perfect place.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mourinho reclama el Balón de Oro para Mbappé
articles.standfirst: "Sabemos quién ha hecho historia este verano y no es del PSG ni de la selección española"
articles.summary: "Sabemos quién ha hecho historia este verano y no es del PSG ni de la selección española"
articles.body: Jose Mourinho tiene claro qué jugador debe ganar el Balón de Oro de 2026. Sin nombrarlo, el entrenador del Madrid reclamó ese premio para uno de los suyos: Kylian Mbappé. El entrenador de Setúbal realizó una larga reflexión para explicar cómo ve un premio que reclama para futbolistas de un perfil muy marcado, alejado de situaciones puntuales y unido a quienes dejan un legado que va mucho más allá de una buena temporada o un gran título. "Es algo muy bonito en lo individual. Entras en la historia individual de un determinado jugador. Esta docena de jugadores de un nivel muy, muy alto, de los cuales tenemos tres o cuatro. Es normal que exista esta ambición. Para mí, el Balón de Oro tiene que ser para esos jugadores que, cuando se retiran, los echamos de menos para la eternidad. Echo de menos a Maradona, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Cristiano, Messi, Zidane, Matthäus... No puedes dar el Balón de Oro porque ganó la Champions o el Mundial. Si quieres premiar la Champions, dale el Balón de Oro a Luis Enrique como mejor entrenador. A España, seguro que De la Fuente lo merece. Esto es el gran homenaje. Otra cosa es el mejor del mundo, no tiene que ser del PSG ni de España. Son dos, tres o cuatro y sabemos quiénes son. Sabemos dónde están, aquí. Sabemos quién ha hecho historia a nivel individual este verano. El Balón de Oro tiene su parte política y, si entra la política, no me gusta tanto. Ya sabemos mi concepto del Balón de Oro. No nos lo vamos a inventar en España o en el PSG. Ahí, Luis Enrique o De la Fuente. El mejor jugador es otro". Esa fue la larga reflexión del entrenador del Madrid. Ese "sabemos quién ha hecho historia a nivel individual este verano" es una idea que ya lanzó el pasado miércoles en la sala de prensa del Bernabéu al ser preguntado por Mbappé. Y su argumento se sostiene en un dato difícil de discutir: desde la pasada Copa del Mundo, el 10 del Madrid es el máximo artillero de la competición, con 22 goles en 22 partidos repartidos en tres ediciones. El mundo de las selecciones tuvo otro punto importante en la rueda de prensa de Mourinho. Este de temor: "Los partidos de selecciones me preocupan. Es mucho tiempo. Los jugadores que van con la selección a jugar me preocupan menos que los que van seleccionados sin jugar. Esos me preocupan muchísimo. Mi relación con Ancelotti hace que esté al corriente de la situación, cambiaremos datos. Con Carlo no será un problema. Con otros con quien no existe esta confianza o amistad, tener jugadores fuera tres semanas es muy complicado. Vamos a tener confianza en la profesionalidad y respeto de esos entrenadores. En el respeto que tengan en los jugadores y los clubes. No quiero dramatizar. Muchas veces hay lesiones con la selección y luego, cuando vuelven al club. Pierden el equilibrio del trabajo que hacían y a las semanas, llega la lesión. Es lo que es y no hay nada que hacer”. En una rueda de prensa en la que anunció la titularidad de Cucurella, puso al equipo por encima de la gran cantidad de juhgadores "muy, muy, muy, muy buenos que tenemos", avisó de que Endrick está muy cerca de volver a jugar ("puede ser ante el Betis), pidió calma a Tchouaméni ("hay que controlar emociones. No quiero que entre, salga, entre, salga") y pusopor las nubes el trabajo de Arbeloa en la cantera del Madrid ("ha hecho un trabajo fantástico abajo. Arriba, la música es otra y ha tenido una situación que no fue fácil"), Mourinho acabó con un mensaje sobre los onces y las posibles filtraciones. “Si mañana vamos al partido y hasta una hora y media antes, el adversario no sabe nuestro equipo, yo prefiero. Pero si hoy sale nuestro equipo, no es dramático. La cosa que preocupa es que cuando tú haces muchos cambios estructurales: si jugamos con tres centrales, con Espi y Kylian juntos... Si hacemos algo que está fuera de lo que el míster del Málaga pueda pensar, ahí sí. Pero la diferencia entre Carreras y Cucurella no me preocupa. El feeling positivo de que no salga es de que nadie ha hablado. Ni los jugadores, ni los utilleros, ni los médicos... Pero sí sale, no es dramático”, aseguró antes de despedirse.

articles.title: Liverpool strike deal to sign PSG’s Barcola for up to $166m: Reports
articles.summary: The 23-year-old French forward would bolster new boss Andoni Iraola’s squad after the departure of Mohamed Salah.
articles.body:
Liverpool have ‌finalised an agreement to sign France forward Bradley ⁠Barcola from ⁠European champions Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth up to 123 million pounds ($166m), media reports said, with the 23-year-old set to become the latest high-profile addition to Andoni Iraola’s squad .

The 20-time English champions ⁠will pay a package worth 106 million pounds ($143m), with add-ons potentially rising to 17 million pounds ($23m), for Barcola, the BBC reported on Saturday. The Athletic reported that he is set to sign a five-year contract.

Barcola joined PSG from his boyhood club Olympique Lyonnais in 2023 and went on to enjoy a trophy-laden spell in the French capital, winning back-to-back Champions League titles in 2024-25 and 2025-26, three Ligue 1 crowns and two French ⁠Cups, among other honours.

He made 152 ⁠appearances in all competitions for PSG, scoring 39 goals and supplying 37 assists.

He had two years remaining on his PSG contract.

Barcola would be the ⁠latest addition to new manager Iraola’s squad following the close-season arrivals of ⁠Uruguayan defender Ronald Araujo on loan, ⁠French centre back Jeremy Jacquet and Spanish forward Victor Munoz.

Liverpool’s attacking options currently include British record signing Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and ‌Munoz as the Merseyside club adjusts to life after talisman Mohamed Salah’s departure . Forward Hugo Ekitike is ‌sidelined ‌with a long-term injury.

Liverpool host Nottingham Forest on Saturday.
